payload.title: Five of the seven acceptance event types the autonomy unlock counts (l1_autonomous_success, l2_supervised_success, l2_autonomous_success, l3_approval_success, critical_violation) have no non-test producer, so the L2 and L3 unlock can never pass and the zero-critical-violation limit counts nothing
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/autonomy_unlock.py:118-125 (the requirement keys the unlock counts, one event type each)
docs/aria/policy/autonomy-unlock.json:10-22 (L2 needs 30 l1_autonomous and 30 l2_supervised successes; L3 adds 10 l2_autonomous, 5 l3_approval and 3 rollback)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/autonomy_unlock.py:282-289 (a critical_violation row blocks every lane, but no code writes one)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/autonomy_ladder.py:84-91 (the only writer of observe_success, run from a manually dispatched burn-in)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/merge_authority.py:162-163 (assert_autonomy_unlocked reads the counts for the merge lane)
payload.rule_violated: ARIA-CRITICAL-015 intent and the autonomy ladder's own policy: a stage must advance on reconciled real outcomes, which needs a producer for every event the policy counts.
payload.notes: git grep at d716541239 for record_acceptance_event finds two non-test call sites: observe_success (autonomy_ladder) and rollback_success (self_revert), and none for the five types above. L2 and L3 unlock can therefore never reach their thresholds whatever merges happen, and a bad ARIA merge cannot be recorded as a critical_violation, so the policy's zero-violation limit is vacuous and only the separate self-merge freeze brakes. The grantable merge lane is held at L1 by runtime_profile.MERGE_LANE_GRANTABLE_LANES, which hides the dead gate today but not the missing violation record. Close condition: own_pr_ci and self_revert (or a new outcome owner) write l1_autonomous_success for a green post-merge ARIA merge and critical_violation for an attributable red or reverted one, and an invariant asserts that every member of ACCEPTANCE_EVENT_TYPES has at least one non-test record_acceptance_event call site (it fails today for five members); a behaviour test records a green lane merge and a reverted lane merge and asserts the two event counts. Verified at origin/main d716541239.
